To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. A novel Cu@AgNas5 with ultrahigh Ag areal loading of 81 mg cm-2 is synthesized by a facile two-step electrochemical nanoengineering process.

Cu supported Ag nanorod arrays (AgNAs) with high loading of Ag (above 81 mg cm -2) and excellent electrocatalytic activity for the oxidation of Zn2+ were successfully prepared by two-step electrochemical nanoengineering.
Cu@Ag nanowires with high Ag loading are prepared by electrochemical nanoengineering method and galvanic replacement reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel Cu supported bimetallic Ag Nanowires as binder-free cathodes for aqueous rechargeble silver zinc batteries with high areal capacity.
the design and preparation of Cu@Ag nanowires (Nas1 5) as binder-free cathode for aqueous rechargebale silver zinc batteries.
the development of a facile, low cost and green method to prepare high performance Cu@AgNas1 5 for rechargeable aqueous batteries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cu supported Ag nanocathodes are promising for high performance rechargeble aqueous batteries.
Cu supported Ag nanorods were prepared by a two-step electrochemical nanoengineering.
the Cu@AgNWs cathode is a promising binder-free cathode for aqueous rechargebale silver zinc battery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the synergistic effect of Cu and Ag in Cu@AgNas1 5 cathode can effectively improve the electrochemical performance of Ag based electrode, and the Cu@AGNas1 6 cathode has the potential to be used in the large scale energy storage system.
we have developed a new type of Cu supported Ag nanorod cathode with ultrahigh loading of above 80 mg cm 2 for high performance rechargeble aqueous silver zinc battery.
Cu supported AgNAs1 2:1, Cu@ AgNAs1:2, Cu@ AgNWs1:2, AgNAs1 and AgNWs1 are prepared by electrochemical nanoengineering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cu@AgNas1 5 can be used as binder free cathode for aqueous rechargeble silver zinc batteries with high areal capacity.
Cu@AgNas1 5 can be used to enhance the performance of aqueous rechargeble batteries, especially the areal capacity.
the Cu@Ag Nanowires are promising binder-free cathodes for high-performance aqueous rechargeable zinc batteries with ultralong cycling stability and ultrahigh arear capacity.
